ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal op-amp circuit. The node at the inverting input is connected to three 1 kΩ branches: the left 5 V source is connected in through 1 kΩ, the upper output V0 is connected in through 1 kΩ feedback, and the lower-left switch B contact is connected in through 1 kΩ. The node at the non-inverting input is connected to two 1 kΩ branches: the left switch A contact is connected in through 1 kΩ, and the lower side is grounded through 1 kΩ. The common terminal of switch SW is connected to a 1 V source and can be connected to position A or B. Reasoning: Under linear negative feedback, an ideal op-amp satisfies V−=V+, and the input current is 0. When SW is in position A, the 1 V source is sent to the non-inverting terminal through 1 kΩ, and at the same time the non-inverting terminal is grounded through 1 kΩ, so V+=1×(1 kΩ/(1 kΩ+1 kΩ))=0.5 V, therefore V−=0.5 V. At this time, the 1 kΩ from the B side to the inverting terminal is open-circuited. Write KCL at the inverting terminal: (V−−5)/1 kΩ+(V−−V0A)/1 kΩ=0. Substituting V−=0.5 V gives (0.5−5)+(0.5−V0A)=0, so V0A=−4 V. When SW is in position B, the non-inverting terminal is grounded only through 1 kΩ, so V+=0, hence V−=0. At this time, the 1 V source is sent to the inverting terminal through the B-side 1 kΩ. Write KCL at the inverting terminal: (0−5)/1 kΩ+(0−1)/1 kΩ+(0−V0B)/1 kΩ=0, giving V0B=−6 V. Therefore V0B/V0A=(−6)/(−4)=1.5.

method.method_draft: For SW in position A, the 1 V source feeds the non-inverting input through 1 kΩ while another 1 kΩ goes to ground, so V+ = 0.5 V and hence V− = 0.5 V. The B-side resistor into the inverting node is open, so KCL at V− with the 5 V input resistor and feedback resistor gives (V−−5)/1k + (V−−V0A)/1k = 0, yielding V0A = -4 V. For SW in position B, the non-inverting input is only tied to ground through 1 kΩ, so V+ = V− = 0. The 1 V source now feeds the inverting input through 1 kΩ, so KCL gives (0−5)/1k + (0−1)/1k + (0−V0B)/1k = 0, yielding V0B = -6 V. Then compute V0B/V0A = (-6)/(-4) = 1.5.

method.method_draft: Build a compact transfer relation for each switch state. In position A, the non-inverting input reference is set by a 1 kΩ–1 kΩ divider from 1 V to ground, so Vref = V+ = 0.5 V. At the inverting node, the connected external source is only 5 V plus the feedback branch, so the equal-resistor relation is V0A = 2Vref − 5 = 2(0.5) − 5 = -4 V. In position B, the non-inverting reference is 0 V because the 1 V lower branch is disconnected and the node is tied to ground through 1 kΩ. The inverting node now sums the 5 V branch and the 1 V branch, with feedback as the third equal branch, so V0B = 3Vref − (5 + 1) = 3(0) − 6 = -6 V. The ratio is therefore V0B/V0A = 1.5.
